Fix a graded $k$-algebra $A$ and let $P$ be a graded left $A$-module
([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). The category
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ of graded left $A$-modules and degree-zero maps is
abelian ([[lem-graded-module-kernels-cokernels-and-biproducts-are-degreewise]]).

**Graded projective.** $P$ is **graded projective** when it is a projective
object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ ([[def-projective-object]]): for every
degree-zero epimorphism $q:E\twoheadrightarrow M$ and every degree-zero
$f:P\to M$ there exists a degree-zero $\widetilde f:P\to E$ with
$q\widetilde f=f$. Thus projectivity is tested only against degree-zero
epimorphisms and degree-zero maps, and the lift need not be unique.

**Finitely generated.** $P$ is **finitely generated as a graded left
$A$-module**, or generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, when for some
$n\ge0$ there are homogeneous elements $p_1,\dots,p_n\in P$ with

$$P=A p_1+\cdots+A p_n .$$

By [[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]] this is the same
notion as finite generation of the underlying $A$-module: a finite homogeneous
family is a finite family, and conversely, if $P=\langle S\rangle_A$ for a
finite set $S$, then writing each $s=\sum_es_e$ as its finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components gives, for every $x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s s\in P$,

$$x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s\sum_es_e=\sum_{s,e}a_s s_e,$$

a finite $A$-linear combination of the homogeneous elements $s_e\in P$; so the
finitely many components of the members of $S$ generate $P$. In particular the
notion does not depend on the chosen finite generating set.

**Finite graded projective.** $P$ is **finite graded projective** when it is
graded projective and generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, that is,
when it is graded projective and finitely generated as an $A$-module. The family
may be empty: $n=0$ gives $P=Ap_1+\cdots+Ap_n=0$, so the zero module is
generated by the empty homogeneous family, and the corresponding finite direct
sum of shifts in the characterization below is the empty direct sum. Its finite
shifted-free characterization is the next result
([[thm-finite-graded-projectives-are-summands-of-finite-graded-free-modules]]),
and it uses this same notion of finite generation throughout: a finite
homogeneous generating family there is exactly a family as above. No choice
principle is used in the equivalence above, which only rewrites a given finite
expression.

Let $k$ be a field and $A$ a finite-dimensional unital associative
$\mathbb Z$-graded $k$-algebra. A **graded-simple module** here means a
nonzero finite-dimensional graded left $A$-module whose only graded submodules
are $0$ and itself. Internal shift acts on graded-simple isomorphism classes
by $[S]\mapsto[S\{r\}]$ for $r\in\mathbb Z$. There are finitely many shift
orbits of graded-simple isomorphism classes. For each orbit choose a
representative $S_i$ and a finite graded projective cover
$p_i:P_i\twoheadrightarrow S_i$, whose kernel is superfluous among graded
submodules. Then

$$
\{[S_i]\}_i\text{ is a }\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]\text{-basis of }G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A), \qquad \{[P_i]\}_i\text{ is a }\mathbb Z[v,v^{-1}]\text{-basis of }K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(A).
$$

In particular, both modules have the same finite rank, the number of graded
simple shift orbits. If $A=0$, both bases are empty and both groups are zero.
No positivity assumption on the grading of $A$ is made.

Let $C_\beta$ be the color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra: on the summand $e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\nu)$ it is the polynomial ring in the elementary symmetric functions of the dots of each color separately. It is central: unequal crossings permute dot positions, and equal-color divided differences $\partial_a$ commute with symmetric polynomials in $x_a,x_{a+1}$ by the Leibniz rule $\partial_a(fg)=\partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)\partial_a(g)$ applied to $s_a$-invariant $f$. In each constant-color block of length $m$ the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ is free over the symmetric subring on the Artin monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_m^{a_m}$, $0\le a_r\le m-r$: adjoining the first root of the universal polynomial $T^m-e_1T^{m-1}+\cdots+(-1)^me_m$ presents $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ as a free rank-$m$ module over the coefficient ring, the corresponding quotient of $T^m-\cdots$ by $T-x_1$ is monic of degree $m-1$ with the correct coefficients, and iteration gives those monomials as a basis while the elementary symmetric functions of the roots recover the $e_r$. Combining with the PBW basis [F1], whose dot monomials factor over the color blocks, gives that $R(\beta)$ is a finite free $C_\beta$-module, of rank $(|\beta|!)^2$ per weight counting the permutation basis; only centrality and this freeness are used below.

(Krull-Schmidt and splitting.) Every finitely generated graded module is bounded below and locally finite by [F1]. Choose finitely many homogeneous generators of degrees $d_j$; evaluation on the generators injects $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ into the finite product of the finitely many finite-dimensional pieces $M_{d_j}$, so every degree-zero endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional, and a nontrivial homogeneous idempotent splits $M$ into two nonzero summands with strictly smaller endomorphism algebras; splitting terminates. For an indecomposable $M$, every endomorphism $f$ satisfies a polynomial minimal equation because $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ is finite-dimensional; factoring it as $T^rg(T)$ with $g(0)\ne0$, Bezout gives a polynomial projector separating the nilpotent part from the invertible part, so indecomposability forces $f$ or $1-f$ to be invertible. Hence the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal, and the usual comparison of two decompositions $\bigoplus p_ii_jp_j=\mathrm{id}$ produces a matching summand and cancellation, proving uniqueness in the degree-zero category; the shifts are recorded as part of each summand.

(Simples and covers.) For a graded simple $S$ and a positive-degree central $c\in C_\beta^+$, the kernel and image of $c$ are graded submodules; if $c$ acted nontrivially it would be injective and hence surjective, contradicting the least nonzero degree of the bounded-below module $S$; so $C_\beta^+S=0$ and $S$ is finite-dimensional because $\bar R=R(\beta)/C_\beta^+R(\beta)$ is finite-dimensional by step 1.1. The finite-dimensional basis theorem [F3] applies to $\bar R$: it has finitely many graded simple shift orbits, and the same then holds for $R(\beta)$, since any simple $R(\beta)$-module is one. Finite decompositions into indecomposables give that $K_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of indecomposable finite graded projectives, with $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$, and finite length of finite-dimensional modules gives that $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the simple shift orbits; both are $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-modules in the sense of [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], the shift action is free because a nonzero finite-dimensional graded module is not isomorphic to a nonzero shift of itself (compare its least and greatest degrees), and the finite-dimensional theorem [F3] gives the same statement for the quotient categories. For a projective cover $P_b$ and simple $S_c$ with their selected shifts, $\operatorname{Hom}(P_b,S_c)=0$ unless $b=c$ at the selected shift, when it equals $\operatorname{End}(S_b)$ by the uniqueness of the cover, computed in the finite-dimensional algebra $\bar R$ where the degree-zero Schur lemma gives $\operatorname{End}(\bar S_b)=k$; this is the diagonal-entry computation of the Hom pairing of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]]. The stronger statement that the diagonal scalar rings equal $k$ over every field, and the associated unscaled dual-basis conclusion, are not inferred here from finite-dimensional algebra alone and are proved separately later on this page; nothing above uses them.

$\Phi_M:=M\otimes_A-$ for the functor that sends a graded left $A$-module $N$ to
the graded left $B$-module $M\otimes_AN$ of the total-degree grading.

1. **Exactness.** If $M$ is flat as an underlying right $A$-module, then
$\Phi_M$ is exact on graded left $A$-modules.

2. **Projectives.** If $M$ is finite graded projective as a left $B$-module,
then $\Phi_M$ carries every finite graded projective left $A$-module to a finite
graded projective left $B$-module.

Neither hypothesis is asserted to imply the other; the companion page exhibits
a right-flat $M$ whose output is not projective and a left-projective $M$ whose
tensor functor is not exact.

Let $A$ and $B$ be graded $k$-algebras, let $M$ be a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule, $X$
a graded left $A$-module and $Y$ a graded left $B$-module. Then currying

$$\Theta:\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(M\otimes_AX,Y)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}\bigl(X,\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)\bigr),\qquad \Theta(F)(x)(m):=F(m\otimes x),$$

is a natural bijection in $X$ and $Y$, where
$\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is the graded left $A$-module of finite sums of
homogeneous $B$-linear maps with the associative action
$(a\cdot f)(m)=f(ma)$. Its inverse sends $f$ to the map $m\otimes x\mapsto
f(x)(m)$ on elementary tensors.

Separately, the same formulas give a natural bijection
$\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M\otimes_AX,Y)\cong
\operatorname{Hom}_A^{\mathrm{ungr}}(X,\operatorname{Hom}_B^{\mathrm{ungr}}(M,Y))$
between ungraded module maps. Here $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ is the direct sum

replaced by one with all ungraded maps on the right.

decomposition of the ordinary tensor product of the underlying abelian groups
$$M\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N\cong\bigoplus_{i,j\in\mathbb Z}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j.$$

$\sum_{i,j}m_i\otimes n_j$, where $m=\sum_i m_i$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$ are their

the identity on homogeneous elementary tensors. Give the summand
$M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$ total degree $i+j$, and write
$G_d:=\bigoplus_{i+j=d}M_i\otimes_{\mathbb Z}N_j$.

ones: for $m=\sum_i m_i$, $a=\sum_\ell a_\ell$ and $n=\sum_jn_j$, the relation

$f_d(p)\in Q_{i+d}$, and comparison of the graded components in $Q$ gives
$f_d(p)=f'_d(p)$ for every $d$ and $p$, so $f_d=f'_d$. Thus
$\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$ is a graded abelian group whose degree-$d$ part is
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,d}(P,Q)$, and the degree-zero morphisms are
$\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(P,Q)$. By definition $\operatorname{HOM}_A(P,Q)$

**The associative left action.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $Y$ a
graded left $B$-module, then $\operatorname{HOM}_B(M,Y)$ carries a left

$$(a\cdot f)(m):=f(ma)\qquad(a\in A,\ m\in M),$$

left $A$-module and an object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$. The same formula
defines an action on the full ungraded $\operatorname{Hom}$ group, where it is
denoted by the same symbol.

derivations.claim: (Shuffle decomposition and freeness.) By [F1] every permutation $w$ of the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ strand positions has a unique decomposition into a product of a block permutation (an element of the parabolic $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$) and a minimal-length shuffle of the two blocks, and their lengths add. The PBW basis of $A$ over $k$, restricted to the source words $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$, therefore exhibits the right $B$-module $eA=eAe$ as the direct sum, over the words $\xi$ and the minimal shuffles $w$, of the principal modules $e(\xi)B$ with their labelled shifts $\delta_R(w,\xi)=\deg(\tau_we(\xi))$ computed from the actual labelled word; horizontal reflection (reversing the order of crossings) produces the analogous left-module decomposition of $Ae$ with shifts $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)=\delta_R(w,w^{-1}\xi)$. Forgetting the gradings, the shuffle monomials for the fixed corner over all words are exactly the $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$ relative positions of the two blocks inside the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ strands, so $eA$ and $Ae$ are free over $B$ of that rank.

(Left adjunction.) For a graded left $B$-module $X$ and a graded left $A$-module $L$, currying gives the natural degree-zero bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(Ae\otimes_BX,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(X,eL)$, $\Phi\mapsto(x\mapsto\Phi(e\otimes x))$, with inverse $f\mapsto(ae\otimes x\mapsto a\,f(x))$, well defined on balanced tensors and inverse by the idempotence of $e$; this is the adjunction of [F3] for the $(A,B)$-bimodule $Ae$.

(Exactness and projectivity.) The right $B$-module $eA$ is free, hence flat, so $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ is exact on graded left modules by [F2]; the functor $\mathrm{Res}=e(-)$ is the multiplication by the idempotent $e$, which is exact because $e(M)=eMe$ and kernels and images of degree-zero maps are computed degreewise in the summands $e(\nu)M$. For the projectivity clauses: if $X$ is a finite graded projective left $B$-module, then $Ae\otimes_BX$ is finite graded projective over $A$ because $Ae$ is a finitely generated projective left $A$-module (it is the image of the idempotent $e$) and [F2] applies to the $(A,B)$-bimodule $M=Ae$; if $P$ is a finite graded projective left $A$-module, then $\mathrm{Res}(P)=eP$ is a direct summand of the finite free module $eA\otimes_BB\cong eA$ tensored with the projective $P$ over $A$, and it is a finite graded projective $B$-module by the same shuffle decomposition of step 1.1. Internal shifts commute with both functors by the shift identities of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]]; this proves the first three clauses.

(Coinduction and the longest shuffle.) The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$ by [F3] applied to $M=eA$, and explicit currying gives $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$. For the second-adjunction formula let $y$ be the longest block shuffle of the two blocks, of degree $-c$ (each of the $|\beta||\gamma|$ crossed positions contributes the negative pairing of the two colours), and let $e'=e(\gamma,\beta)$ be the reversed-block idempotent. By PBW there is a well-defined $B$-balanced coefficient map $t:eAe'\to B$ projecting onto the $y$-coefficient, where the reversed block order is read in $B$ through the flip equivalence $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)\to R(\gamma)\otimes_kR(\beta)$; dot slides and block crossings preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient, while every dot or braid correction in a shorter shuffle has strictly smaller shuffle length and is killed by $t$. Hence the map $\Phi:Ae'\to\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)$, $z\mapsto(u\mapsto t(uz))$, is a degree-$c$ map of $(A,B)$-bimodules, and it is compatible with the flip identification.

(Mackey filtration.) Fix a second flag with idempotent $e'=e(\beta',\gamma')$ and choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row block permutation group and the column block permutation group acting on the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ positions. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner $eAe'$ by the four intersection blocks $(a,b;c,d)$ with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, and filter by the crossing length of the double-coset representatives. The span of the double cosets of strictly smaller length is a $(B,B')$-sub-bimodule: sliding a block generator across a representative either stays in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or produces a quadratic/braid correction of strictly smaller length, which lies in the smaller span. In the associated quotient only the monomials whose permutation is the minimal double-coset representative survive; they are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases of the four blocks composed with the row and column induced bimodules and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks, which carries the shift $-(b\mid c)$ because the crossed colours are precisely $b$ and $c$. The basis bijection defines inverse maps between the associated quotient and the composite four-block restriction/induction bimodule, so the filtration is proved and not merely a character identity; iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block statement.

(Triangularity and the functor formula.) Pair the left shuffle basis of $Ae'$ with the right shuffle basis of $eA$ by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, the coefficient matrix of the pairing $u\mapsto t(uz)$ is triangular: a complementary pair is exactly the reduced longest shuffle with coefficient $1$ up to the absorbed equal-colour signs, and a noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic or braid correction to strictly smaller length, hence vanishes in the associated graded. Finite triangular elimination over $B$ (division by the diagonal units $1$) inverts the matrix, so $\Phi$ is an isomorphism of graded $(A,B)$-bimodules; consequently $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\cong Ae'\{c\}$ with the $B$-action transported by the block flip. Since $eA$ is finite projective over $B$ by step 1.1, evaluation identifies $\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)\otimes_BX\cong\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,X)$ for every graded $B$-module $X$ (checked on finite free modules and finite summands), and tracking the outer right $B$-action through the flip gives the functorial isomorphism $\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}$.

All clauses of the statement are now proved: step 1.1 gives the freeness and the labelled shuffle shifts, step 2.1 the exactness, shift compatibility and projective preservation, step 1.2 the left adjunction, steps 2.2 and 3.1 the right adjoint and its exact reversed-block formula, and step 2.3 the finite Mackey filtration and its multi-block version.

The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$, with $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$, and the exact generic second-adjunction formula is
$$\mathrm{Coind}_{\beta,\gamma}(M\boxtimes N)\cong\mathrm{Ind}_{\gamma,\beta}(N\boxtimes M)\{c\}.$$

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and $\beta\in Q_+$.
(i) Every finitely generated graded left $R(\beta)$-module has a decomposition into finitely many indecomposable graded modules, unique as a finite multiset of degree-zero graded isomorphism classes, including the actual shifts of their summands; in particular the category $\mathrm{GrMod}_0R(\beta)$ of finitely generated graded modules has the Krull-Schmidt property.
(ii) Every simple graded $R(\beta)$-module is finite-dimensional, killed by the augmentation ideal $\mathrm{Sym}^+(\beta)$ of the CENTRAL color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$; up to isomorphism and shift there are finitely many, and each has a projective cover which is finitely generated.
(iii) The split Grothendieck group $K_0(R(\beta))$ of finite graded projective modules is a free $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-module: the classes of the indecomposable finitely generated graded projectives, modulo grading shifts, form a basis with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$; equivalently the classes of all finitely generated indecomposable graded projectives form a shift-orbit basis. Similarly $G_0(R(\beta))$ is free on the shift orbits of simple modules, and the Hom pairing of projective covers and simples has diagonal entries $\dim_k\operatorname{End}^0(S_b)$, with the selected cover/simple shifts, under the Hom convention of [[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]].

derivations.claim: (Nil-Hecke tail and its matrix units.) The constant-colour block $R(r\alpha_i)=NH_r$ is the nil-Hecke algebra, and the explicit Artin polynomial/matrix-unit description exhibits it as a graded matrix algebra $\mathrm{Mat}_{r!}(k)$ with its unique graded simple $L(i^r)$ absolutely simple; the divided-projective idempotent of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]] cuts out a one-dimensional image, so $L(i^r)$ has a projective cover with $\operatorname{End}^0=k$. If $T$ is a finite-dimensional simple module over $R(\mu)\otimes_kNH_r$, then the positive symmetric functions of the tail dots are central and positive, so they act on $T$ by $0$ (a nonzero positive-degree central endomorphism of a finite-dimensional simple module is invertible, hence has a nonzero eigenvalue with a least-degree contradiction); hence $T$ is killed by the augmentation ideal of the tail center and the matrix-unit decomposition of $NH_r$ writes $T=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with $N$ a graded simple $R(\mu)$-module, unique up to shift.

(Maximal restriction.) Let $S$ be a finite-dimensional graded simple with $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$ maximal. The finite-dimensional module $\Delta_i^rS$ is nonzero by the definition of $\epsilon_i$ and has a simple submodule; by step 1.1 it is of the form $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ for a graded simple $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$. If $N$ carried a word ending in $i$, then concatenating any nonzero nil-Hecke tail word would produce a nonzero vector in $S$ of tail $r+1$, contradicting maximality, so $\epsilon_i(N)=0$. By the left adjunction of [F2] the inclusion $N\boxtimes L(i^r)\hookrightarrow\Delta_i^rS$ corresponds to a nonzero map $M:=\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))\to S$, which is surjective since $S$ is simple. In the Mackey filtration of $\Delta_i^rM$ every shuffle bringing $t>0$ colours $i$ from the first block into the final tail contains a factor $\Delta_i^tN$ and is zero; the only surviving filtration quotient is $N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ with zero crossing shift, so $\Delta_i^rM=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ exactly. This is a one-surviving-quotient computation, not a semisimplicity assumption.

(Unique head and simplicity.) Every nonzero quotient $Q$ of $M$ has nonzero defining corner: if $eQ=0$ with $e=e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)$, then the composite $Ae\otimes_B(N\boxtimes L(i^r))\to M\to Q$ is zero by the tensor/Res adjunction, hence $Q=0$. The finite graded semisimple head of $M$ therefore has exactly one simple summand, occurring once, because its exact $e$-restriction is a quotient of the simple $eM=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; this head is $S$, and $eM\to eS$ is an isomorphism, so exactness gives $e\ker(M\to S)=0$ and every other composition factor of $M$ has smaller tail. Underlying and absolute simplicity of $S$: induct on the height of $\beta$. For positive height choose $i$ with $r>0$; by step 2.1 and induction $N$ and $L(i^r)$ are absolutely simple, so $eS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$ has endomorphism ring $k$; if $U\le S$ is any ungraded submodule with $eU\ne0$, then $eU=eS$ and $U=S$ because $S$ is generated by $eS$; if $eU=0$, the graded submodule generated by the homogeneous components of vectors of $U$ is nonzero, killed by $e$, and hence equal to $S$ by graded simplicity, contradicting $eS\ne0$. Thus $S$ is simple as an ungraded module, and every $R$-endomorphism of $S$ is determined on $eS$, giving $\operatorname{End}_R(S)=k$. The finite-density matrix argument then shows absolute simplicity over every field: any $m$ linearly independent vectors can be sent to arbitrary targets by one algebra element, by induction on $m$ and the commutant $k$ clause, so the action realizes all $k$-linear matrices and remains simple after field extension.

(Triangular divided-string basis.) Choose a cyclic order of the finite colour support and recursively strip maximal $i$-tails, producing for each simple shift orbit a finite tuple $Y_b$ of ordered divided powers; two simples with the same tuple agree by the unique-head recursion of step 3.1. Form $P(Y_b)$ from the reversed ordered normalized divided blocks. Its homogeneous Hom to $S_c$ is the corresponding product of divided idempotents acting on $S_c$; comparing tuples lexicographically, if $Y_b>Y_c$ at the first differing entry then the required tail exceeds the maximal tail of the successively stripped simple $S_c$, and the corner is zero. When the tuples agree, every maximal restriction is the simple tensor computed in step 2.1 and each nil-Hecke divided idempotent reduces the tail to one dimension, so by induction the diagonal Hom is a single Laurent monomial with coefficient $1$. Shifting each $S_b$ makes the diagonal $1$. The finite matrix is triangular over $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ with diagonal $1$; Krull-Schmidt and the projective-cover/simple Hom pairing (now with $\operatorname{End}(S)=k$ from step 3.1) identify it with the matrix expressing the projective classes in the cover basis, and successive integral triangular elimination proves that the selected classes $[P(Y_b)]$ are an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; the whole family of divided words spans because the recursion covers every simple, while redundancy of non-selected words is allowed. This completes the integral surjectivity argument without a PBW rank or flat-family shortcut.

(First-color version.) For maximal FIRST-color blocks use the defining idempotent $e(r\alpha_i,\mu)$ and $M=\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$ with $\epsilon_i^L(N)=0$; a simple submodule of the maximal first-block restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}S$ has the form $L(i^r)\boxtimes N$ by the same nil-Hecke matrix units of step 1.1, and any first-colour support of $N$ would extend the maximal first block, so it vanishes. In the Mackey restriction of $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}M$ every nontrivial shuffle bringing a positive number $t$ of $i$-colours from $N$ into the first block contains $\Delta_i^{(L,t)}N$ and is zero, so the sole uncrossed quotient is $L(i^r)\boxtimes N$ with shift $0$; the defining-corner generation and exact-head argument of steps 3.1 and 3.1 are unchanged. Thus the first-block assertions are proved directly, with no unsigned star-crystal preservation assumed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Assume AC; it is used only to apply the two-sided coideal lemma in step 3.1. For an indeterminate $q'$, let $U_{q'}\mathfrak n^+$ be the algebra over $\mathbb C(q')$ with the same generators and positive quantum Serre relations, with $q_i'=q'^{d_i}$. Then:

(i) The composite $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+\to U_\hbar\mathfrak b^+\xrightarrow{p_\hbar}\mathcal V$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras onto $\langle V\rangle$. In particular, $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$ is a free $R$-module and each root-graded component $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]$ is a finite-rank free $R$-module.

(ii) The classical limit is the classical half: $U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+/\hbar U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+\cong U\mathfrak n^+$ as $\mathbb N^I$-graded algebras, by $e_i\mapsto\bar e_i$.

(iii) For every $\alpha\in Q_+$,
$$\operatorname{rank}_{R}U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U\mathfrak n^+[\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(q')}U_{q'}\mathfrak n^+[\alpha].$$

derivations.claim: (Induction algebra and restriction coalgebra.) The induction product is associative and unital: the balanced identifications of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] for the two parenthesizations of three blocks are inverse degree-zero isomorphisms, and the unit is $[R(0)]=[k]$. Restriction is coassociative with counit the weight-zero component, because iterated idempotent restriction multiplies the corresponding block idempotents, and the two orders of multiplication agree. To prove that $[\mathrm{Res}]$ respects the twisted multiplication, apply the Mackey filtration [F1] to the corner $e_{\beta,\gamma}Re_{\beta',\gamma'}$: PBW partitions its basis by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length, and multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms; the associated quotient is exactly the four-block restriction/induction bimodule shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives $[\mathrm{Res}](xy)=\sum q^{-(|y_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ with the twisted product, so $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism; no use of the second adjunction is needed.

(Contraction complex for the Serre relation.) Fix $i\ne j$, put $d=-a_{ij}$, $D=d+1$ and $N=D+1=d+2$. For $0\le r\le D$ take the divided-projective corner of the word $i^rj i^{D-r}$, using its two nil-Hecke idempotents, and apply the shift normalizing $P_{i,r}$ and $P_{i,D-r}$. The neighbouring maps are right multiplication by the crossing strings moving $j$ across one $i$-block, cut by these idempotents: in the printed notation of the source, $e_{r+1}$ cuts the $r$-th corner and $\alpha_{r,r+1}=e_{r+1}\tau_{N-1}\cdots\tau_{r+1}e_{r+2}$, $\alpha_{r+1,r}=e_{r+2}\tau_1\cdots\tau_{r+1}e_{r+1}$. Consecutive forward maps compose to zero because a repeated $i$-crossing hits the nil-Hecke symmetrizing idempotent. Expanding $Q_{ij}(u,v)=\sum t_{ab}u^av^b$, the braid relation makes the difference of the neighbouring forward and backward compositions equal to the divided difference of $Q_{ij}$ in the two outer $i$-variables; the same-colour divided differences at the ends extract only the term $u^d$, because all terms of $u$-degree $<d$ vanish and the weighted homogeneity excludes $u$-degree $>d$. Its coefficient $t_{d0}$ is a unit by (Q4). Rescaling each backward map by that unit and the alternating sign produces maps $h$ with $dh+hd=1$ on the finite complex. The fixed native sign $\tau=-\tau_{\text{source}}$ changes the crossing strings by explicit length signs, which are absorbed in the backward rescalings, leaving the same contracting identity; the normalized shifts make every neighbouring differential degree zero. This is the contracting calculation of Rouquier’s divided-power contraction lemma, valid over the universal coefficient ring and hence after every specialization of $Q$.

(Alternating classes and the $a_{ij}=0$ case.) A bounded complex with $dh+hd=1$ is split contractible: choosing the successive splittings gives a contraction with $h^2=0$, and then $d+h$ is an isomorphism from even to odd part; hence the alternating sum of the classes of its terms vanishes, which is exactly $\sum_{a+b=D}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}][P_{j,1}][P_{i,b}]=0$, the displayed Serre relation. If $a_{ij}=0$ then the crossing $\tau$ of the two colours is invertible (its square is the nonzero constant $Q_{ij}$), and right multiplication by it gives a degree-zero isomorphism between the two corners, so $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{ij}]=[P_{ji}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$.

(Descent of $\gamma$.) First define $\gamma$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ from the presentation of the negative Serre half: [F3] identifies the abstract divided-power algebra with its shuffle model, and the assignments $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$, extended multiplicatively and $q$-linearly, respect all Serre relations by step 3.1 and the commuting relation, so they define an algebra homomorphism $\gamma_{\mathbb Q}$ on the localization. Since the $A$-form is the $A$-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words [F2], and the divided-word images lie in $K_0(R)$, the homomorphism restricts to the stated $A$-linear $\gamma$; the formula $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$ is multiplicativity of $\gamma$ together with the definition of $P_\theta$. Coproduct compatibility is the Mackey computation of step 1.1, and bar compatibility is the projective $^\#$ duality of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], which fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ and hence each word class. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve projective ranks.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $\psi$ be the horizontal-reflection anti-involution of $R(\beta)$ (reflection of diagrams about a horizontal axis, which reverses the order of crossings); for a finite graded left module $P$ let $P^{\psi}$ be the right module with $p\cdot r:=\psi(r)p$. For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finite graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. Both are additive, vanish on different-weight components, and descend to $K_0(R)=\bigoplus_\beta K_0(R(\beta))$: the tensor form is $A$-bilinear and the Hom form is $A$-sesquilinear (first variable conjugate-linear), with values in $\mathbb Q(q)$, more precisely in the localization adjoining all $(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$; the values lie in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q$ because $P^\psi\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q$ is a finite free graded module over the central color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra $C_\beta$ of [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Normalization: $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q^{2d_i})^{-1}=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and $([P_i],[P_j])=0$ for $i\ne j$, where $P_i=R(\alpha_i)$.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $Af$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i'$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$\varepsilon\colon U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the **augmentation**, the projection
onto the degree-zero component $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\cdot1$ (so
$\varepsilon(Q)=0$ on all positive-height components and $\varepsilon(1)=1$).

The **normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form** on $U_q^-$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon U_q^-\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(H) $B$ is **homogeneous**: $B\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu]\bigr)=0$ whenever
$\nu\ne\mu$;

(N) $B(1,1)=1$;

(R) $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ for all $i\in I$ and all $P,Q\in U_q^-$.

Equivalently, axioms (H) and (N) may be replaced by the single **counit
normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

in the presence of (R) (Verification, step 1.1).

Axioms (H) and (N) (equivalently (C)) are essential and not redundant: the
recursion (R) together with $B(1,1)=1$ alone neither forces symmetry nor
uniqueness, as the rank-one witness of step 3.1 shows.

The axioms determine $B$ uniquely: peeling first letters in the first argument
writes every positive-height $P$ as a finite sum $P=\sum_iF_iP_i$ and evaluates
$B(P,Q)=\sum_iB(P_i,e_i'Q)$, reducing the height; the base of the induction is
(C) (Verification, step 2.1). The **existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy** of
$B$ on $U_q^-$ for the actual quotient by the Serre ideal are not proved here:
they are the content of the negative-half form theorem
`thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral`,
the declared justification of this definition, which also settles the exact
integrality normalization ($A$-valuedness on the word lattice and the
Gaussian-factorial denominators on the divided-power lattice). That theorem
is proved on this page, and its statement is the declared supplier of
existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy; this definition itself claims only that
(H), (N) and (R) determine $B$ and that the normalization cannot be relaxed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation in the parameter $v$ with $v_i=q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}=K_{-h}$, extended semilinearly ( $\varphi(\lambda x)=\lambda|_{q\mapsto q^{-1}}\varphi(x)$ ) and multiplicatively, is a semilinear algebra involution of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: it carries every source relation above to a relation of the library presentation and conversely, so it identifies the two presentations and is the bar involution $\psi$; and $\varphi(U_A)=U_A$ with $\varphi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)}$, $\varphi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)}$, $\varphi(K_h^{\pm1})=K_h^{\mp1}$, $\varphi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: (KLR side.) The tensor form is symmetric and bilinear and takes the value $([P_i],[P_i])=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ on the rank-one divided powers by [F1]. By the adjunction of Ind and Res and the exact Mackey comparison, it satisfies $(x,yy')=(r(x),y\otimes y')$ with $r=[\mathrm{Res}]$ whenever $x,y,y'$ are classes of finite graded projectives: $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathrm{Ind}(P\boxtimes Q),R)\cong\mathrm{Hom}(P\boxtimes Q,eR)$ gives the comparison, and the corner restriction has the finite filtration of [F2].

(Abstract side.) $B_K$ is characterized by (H), (N), (R) of [F3], and its normalized multiple $B_L=C_\nu B_K$ satisfies the generator value $B_L(\theta_i,\theta_j)=\delta_{ij}(1-q_i^2)^{-1}$ and the recursion $B_L(F_iP,Q)=(1-q_i^2)^{-1}B_L(P,e_i'Q)$ by [F4]; the same recursion with the same base value determines every value on word monomials inductively, since peeling the first letter of the first argument and applying the recursion reduces the positive height by one.

(Comparison on monomials.) The KLR pairing and $B_L$ satisfy the same recursion and the same value at $1$: on the KLR side this is step 1.1 with $\gamma(F_i)=\gamma(\theta_i)=[P_{i,1}]=[P_i]$ and the identification of the restriction class with the coproduct; on the abstract side it is step 1.2. Induction on the height of the weight components therefore gives $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))_{KLR}=B_L(x,y)$ on all divided-power monomials and hence on all of $Af$ by bilinearity, using that $\gamma$ is onto the classes of the divided words by [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]. Injectivity of $\gamma$ is not used: the equality is checked on the spanning monomials.

(Nondegeneracy and generator values.) By [F5] the form $B_K$, hence the unit multiple $B_L$, is nondegenerate on each finite weight component, so the KLR tensor pairing is nondegenerate there as well; the Axiom of Choice enters only through this supplier, and the categorical comparison of steps 1.1, 1.2 and 2.1 is choice-free. The Hom-form identity $(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))'=B_L(\overline{x},y)$ follows from $h(P,Q)=T(P^\#,Q)$ of [[def-the-klr-cartan-pairing]] and the bar compatibility of $B_L$ with the twisted Hom duality ([[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]). For the rank-one divided power, $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ gives $([P_{i,n}],[P_{i,n}])=\prod_{a=1}^n(1-q_i^{2a})^{-1}$, matching $B_L(\theta_i^{(n)},\theta_i^{(n)})$ by the recursion of step 1.2; for $n=1$ this is the generator value already recorded.

For a finite-dimensional graded module $M$ of weight $\beta$ set $\epsilon_i(M)=\max\{r:e(\beta-r\alpha_i,r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$. If $S$ is simple and $r=\epsilon_i(S)>0$, there is a simple graded $R(\beta-r\alpha_i)$-module $N$ with $\epsilon_i(N)=0$ such that $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$, where $L(i^r)$ is the unique nil-Hecke simple up to shift. Conversely, for any such $N$, $\mathrm{Ind}(N\boxtimes L(i^r))$ has a unique simple graded head $S$, appearing once as a composition factor, with $\epsilon_i(S)=r$ and $\Delta_i^rS=N\boxtimes L(i^r)$; every other composition factor has smaller $i$-tail. The graded simples of every $R(\beta)$ remain simple without grading and are absolutely simple; all ordinary endomorphisms are $k$ and nonzero homogeneous endomorphisms have degree $0$. The classes of normalized simples and their projective covers are therefore unscaled dual shift-orbit bases for the projective/simple Hom pairing. For each $\beta$ there is a finite family of ordered divided-power words $Y_b$ whose normalized projective classes pair triangularly with the simple classes, with diagonal entries $1$ after choosing the simple grading shifts. Thus the selected $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$; arbitrary divided words span, but need not be a basis. The identical statements hold for maximal FIRST-color blocks, with $\epsilon_i^L(M)=\max\{r:e(r\alpha_i,\beta-r\alpha_i)M\ne0\}$, restriction $\Delta_i^{(L,r)}$ and induction $\mathrm{Ind}(L(i^r)\boxtimes N)$.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $Q$ be a KLR datum as in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] and let $K_0(R):=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}K_0(R(\beta))$ be the split Grothendieck group of finite graded projective modules with the shift action $q[P]=[P\{1\}]$ ([[def-split-grothendieck-group-of-an-additive-category]], [[def-graded-grothendieck-group-shift-module-and-cartan-map]], [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]).
(i) The induction product $[P][P']:=[\mathrm{Ind}_{\beta,\gamma}(P\boxtimes P')]$ for $P\in K_0(R(\beta)),P'\in K_0(R(\gamma))$ makes $K_0(R)$ a unital associative $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-algebra, and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ makes it a coassociative counital $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-coalgebra; with the twisted multiplication on $K_0(R)\otimes K_0(R)$ defined by $(x_1\otimes x_2)(x_1'\otimes x_2')=q^{-(|x_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ on homogeneous elements, $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism ([[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]]).
(ii) With the divided-power projectives $P_{i,n}$ of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], the classes $[P_{i,n}]$ satisfy, for all $i\ne j$, the divided-power quantum Serre relation
$$\sum_{a+b=-a_{ij}+1}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}]\,[P_{j,1}]\,[P_{i,b}]=0\qquad\text{in }K_0(R),$$
with the convention $[P_{i,0}]=1$, and satisfy $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$ when $a_{ij}=0$; these are the defining relations of the negative half.
(iii) Consequently the assignment $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$ extends uniquely to an algebra homomorphism $\gamma:Af\to K_0(R)$ of the divided-power form of the negative half, with $\gamma(\theta_i^{(n)})=[P_{i,n}]$ and $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$; $\gamma$ is compatible with the coproducts ($r$ on $Af$ and $[\mathrm{Res}]$ on $K_0(R)$) and with the bar involutions, and it is $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-linear.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation in the parameter $v$ with $v_i=q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}=K_{-h}$, extended semilinearly ( $\varphi(\lambda x)=\lambda|_{q\mapsto q^{-1}}\varphi(x)$ ) and multiplicatively, is a semilinear algebra involution of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: it carries every source relation above to a relation of the library presentation and conversely, so it identifies the two presentations and is the bar involution $\psi$; and $\varphi(U_A)=U_A$ with $\varphi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)}$, $\varphi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)}$, $\varphi(K_h^{\pm1})=K_h^{\mp1}$, $\varphi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

derivations.claim: (Surjectivity.) By [F1] the classes $[P(Y_b)]$ form an $A$-basis of $K_0(R(\beta))$ for a finite family of ordered divided-power words; each $Y_b$ is a word in divided powers of single colours, so its class equals $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})$ by multiplicativity of $\gamma$ and the definition of $P_\theta$. Hence every class in $K_0(R(\beta))$ is an $A$-linear combination of classes $[P_\theta]$ of divided-power projectives, and $\gamma$ is onto.

(Injectivity.) Suppose $\gamma(x)=0$ for some $x\in Af_\nu$. By [F2] and [F3], for every $y$ in the same weight component one has $B_L(x,y)=(\gamma(x),\gamma(y))=0$; since $B_L$ is a unit multiple of the nondegenerate form $B_K$ on the finite-dimensional $\mathbb Q(q)$-space $Af_\nu\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)$, this forces $x=0$. The categorical and form-comparison steps of [F2] are choice-free; the Axiom of Choice is inherited only through the nondegeneracy supplier [F3].

(Compatibility and ranks.) The intertwining of multiplications is multiplicativity of $\gamma$ together with the induction formula of [[thm-klr-projective-grothendieck-group-satisfies-the-negative-quantum-serre-relations]]; the intertwining of comultiplications is the Mackey comparison of [[thm-klr-induction-and-restriction-are-biadjoint-and-preserve-projectives]] against the coproduct $r$ of the negative half; the bar compatibility is $P_{i,n}^\#=P_{i,n}$ for the normalized divided projectives of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], and form preservation is [F2]. Since $\gamma$ is an isomorphism of $A$-modules by steps 1.1 and 2.1, the free $A$-rank of $K_0(R(\beta))$ equals that of $Af_\beta$; the finiteness of both ranks follows from the triangular basis and from the degreewise freeness of $Af$ [F4], and the infinite-dimensional algebra $R(\beta)$ itself is not compared with $f_\beta$.
